overview.intro:
Chapter 59 covers textile fabrics that have been **impregnated, coated, covered or laminated** — with plastics (heading 5903: PVC- and PU-coated fabrics, faux leather, tarpaulin and banner fabric), with rubber (5906) or with gum or starch (5901: book cloth, tracing cloth, artist canvas) — plus **tire cord fabric** (5902), linoleum, textile wall coverings, wicks, textile hose, **conveyor and transmission belts** (5910) and the **technical textiles** of heading 5911: paper-machine felts and forming fabrics, bolting cloth, filter cloth, printers' blankets, gaskets and other machinery parts. Base rates are moderate: 51 of the 75 tariff lines are dutiable, from 2.6% to **14.1%** (layered PVC-coated man-made-fiber fabrics); tire cord pays 5.8%, most coated man-made-fiber fabrics 7.5%–8%.

The U.S. imported **$2.86B** of these goods in 2025, 8.8% less than in 2024. **Mexico** ($485M) was the largest supplier — mostly technical textiles of 5911 — ahead of **India** ($315M, mostly plastic-coated fabrics), Canada, China and **Vietnam**, which shipped $185M of tire cord fabric. On top of the base rate comes the **extra duty by country**: since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 tariff on 60 economies — +10% for India, Cambodia and the UK, +12.5% for Vietnam, Turkey and Israel, **10% in total** for EU and Taiwanese goods and 12.5% in total for Japanese and Korean goods. **China pays +12.5% plus +25% (List 3)** on every line but one, so Chinese PU-coated fabric pays 45%. USMCA-qualifying goods from Mexico pay nothing; four Canadian subheadings — two plastic-coated fabric lines, 5907.00.60 and 5911.90.00 — owe a **50% Section 338 duty even under USMCA**. Three antidumping cases reach the chapter: primed artist canvas from China, narrow woven ribbons from China and Taiwan, and laminated woven sack fabric from China and Vietnam.

productGroups.label: Book cloth, tracing cloth, prepared painting canvas & buckram
productGroups.blurb: Fabrics coated with gum or starch for book covers, tracing cloth, prepared painting canvas and buckram: 7% for man-made fibers, 4.1% for cotton and other fibers. Primed artist canvas from China also carries an antidumping duty (order A-570-899).

productGroups.label: Tire cord fabric of nylon, polyester or rayon
productGroups.blurb: Tire cord fabric of high-tenacity nylon or polyester yarn pays 5.8%; rayon and other tire cord is Free. Vietnam supplied $185M of the $298M imported in 2025.

productGroups.label: Fabrics coated or laminated with plastics (PVC, PU — incl. faux leather)
productGroups.blurb: The rate follows the plastic, the fiber and the plastic content: cotton 2.7%; man-made-fiber fabrics coated with PVC, PU or other plastics 7.5%, or 8% (PU) and 14.1% (PVC) for the layered fabrics of Section XI note 9; Free when the fabric is over 70% rubber or plastics by weight (over 60% plastics for the note 9 fabrics). Faux leather, tarpaulin and banner fabric are here.

productGroups.label: Linoleum & floor coverings on a textile backing
productGroups.blurb: Linoleum and floor coverings made of a coating on a textile backing are Free from every column 1 country.

productGroups.label: Textile wall coverings
productGroups.blurb: Textile wall coverings in rolls at least 45 cm wide are Free, whether backed with paper or not.

productGroups.label: Rubberized fabrics & rubberized adhesive tape
productGroups.blurb: Rubberized adhesive tape up to 20 cm wide pays 2.9%; other rubberized fabrics 2.7% (cotton), 3.3% (other fibers), 7.5% (knitted man-made fibers) or Free (man-made fibers over 70% rubber, and other woven man-made fibers).

productGroups.label: Other coated fabrics & painted theatrical scenery
productGroups.blurb: Laminated fabrics and Section XI note 9 fabrics of man-made fibers pay 8%; painted theatrical scenery and other coated or impregnated fabrics (for example flocked or silicone-treated) are Free.

productGroups.label: Textile wicks & gas mantle fabric
productGroups.blurb: Woven, plaited or knitted wicks for lamps, stoves, lighters and candles, and gas mantle fabric: 3.4%.

productGroups.label: Textile hose (fire hose and similar tubing)
productGroups.blurb: Textile hosepiping and tubing, such as lay-flat fire hose: Free if of vegetable fibers, 3.3% otherwise.

productGroups.label: Textile conveyor & transmission belts
productGroups.blurb: Conveyor and transmission belts and belting of textile material: 4% of man-made fibers (V-belts, synchronous belts, belting), 2.6% otherwise. Belts of rubber-coated fabric are rubber belts of heading 4010 (Chapter 59 note 7).

productGroups.label: Technical textiles: paper-machine clothing, bolting cloth, filter cloth, printers' blankets
productGroups.blurb: Technical textiles: paper-machine felts and forming fabrics 3.8%, printers' rubberized blankets 2.9%, screen-printing fabric 3.3%, other bolting cloth Free, filter cloth for oil presses 8%, gaskets, packing cords and other machinery parts of textile 3.8%.

workedExamples.title: Polyester tire cord fabric from Vietnam
workedExamples.body: Tire cord fabric of high-tenacity polyester yarn pays 5.8%. Vietnam adds +12.5% (9903.05.84): **18.3%**, $1,830 on a $10,000 shipment. The same fabric pays 43.3% from China (5.8% + 12.5% + 25% List 3), 15.8% from India and 12.5% in total from South Korea (KORUS removes the 5.8%, and the Korean rate tops the total up to 12.5%). Tire cord fabric is not on the Section 232 auto-parts list.

workedExamples.title: PU-coated polyester fabric (faux leather) from China
workedExamples.body: Man-made-fiber fabric coated with polyurethane, under 70% plastics by weight, pays 7.5%. China adds +12.5% (9903.05.31) and +25% (List 3, 9903.88.03): **45%**, $4,500 on $10,000. From Taiwan it pays 10% in total, from Vietnam 20%, from India 17.5%. Coating Chinese greige fabric in another country does not by itself change its origin (19 CFR 102.21).

workedExamples.title: Plastic-coated man-made-fiber fabric from Canada
workedExamples.body: The base rate is 7.5%, and USMCA-qualifying goods are exempt from the 10% Section 301 duty (9903.05.93). But 5903.90.25 is on the Section 338 list in U.S. note 51(b)(3) (9903.03.14), and that 50% applies even when USMCA is claimed: **$5,000** on a $10,000 shipment. A non-qualifying shipment pays 7.5% + 10% + 50% = 67.5%.

workedExamples.title: Paper-machine press felt from Germany
workedExamples.body: Press felts of 650 g/m² or more pay 3.8%. For EU goods with a base rate under 10%, the 2026 Section 301 action charges 10% in total (9903.05.38–9903.05.39), so a $100,000 felt pays **$10,000** instead of $3,800. From Japan it pays 12.5% in total, from Mexico nothing under USMCA.

**Note 1.** Except where the context otherwise requires, for the purposes of this chapter the expression "textile fabrics" applies only to the woven fabrics of chapters 50 to 55 and headings 5803 and 5806, the braids and ornamental trimmings in the piece of heading 5808 and the knitted or crocheted fabrics of headings 6002 to 6006.

**Note 2.** Heading 5903 applies to: (a) textile fabrics, impregnated, coated, covered or laminated with plastics, whatever the weight per square meter and whatever the nature of the plastic material (compact or cellular), other than: (1) fabrics in which the impregnation, coating or covering cannot be seen with the naked eye (usually chapters 50 to 55, 58 or 60), no account being taken of any resulting change of color; (2) products which cannot, without fracturing, be bent manually around a cylinder of a diameter of 7 mm, at a temperature between 15°C and 30°C (usually chapter 39); (3) products in which the textile fabric is either completely embedded in plastics or entirely coated or covered on both sides with such material, provided that such coating or covering can be seen with the naked eye (chapter 39); (4) fabrics partially coated or partially covered with plastics and bearing designs resulting from these treatments (usually chapters 50 to 55, 58 or 60); (5) plates, sheets or strip of cellular plastics, combined with textile fabric, where the textile fabric is present merely for reinforcing purposes (chapter 39); or (6) textile products of heading 5811; (b) fabrics made from yarn, strip or the like, impregnated, coated, covered or sheathed with plastics, of heading 5604.

**Note 3.** For heading 5903, "textile fabrics laminated with plastics" means products made by the assembly of one or more layers of fabrics with one or more sheets or film of plastics which are combined by any process that bonds the layers together, whether or not the sheets or film of plastics are visible to the naked eye in the cross-section.

**Note 4.** For heading 5905, "textile wall coverings" applies to products in rolls, of a width of not less than 45 cm, suitable for wall or ceiling decoration, consisting of a textile surface which has been fixed on a backing or has been treated on the back (impregnated or coated to permit pasting). It does not apply to wall coverings of textile flock or dust fixed directly on a backing of paper (heading 4814) or on a textile backing (generally heading 5907).

**Note 5.** For heading 5906, "rubberized textile fabrics" means: (a) textile fabrics impregnated, coated, covered or laminated with rubber, weighing not more than 1,500 g/m², or weighing more than 1,500 g/m² and containing more than 50 percent by weight of textile material; (b) fabrics made from yarn, strip or the like, impregnated, coated, covered or sheathed with rubber, of heading 5604; and (c) fabrics composed of parallel textile yarns agglomerated with rubber, irrespective of their weight per square meter. The heading does not apply to plates, sheets or strip of cellular rubber combined with textile fabric present merely for reinforcing purposes (chapter 40), or textile products of heading 5811.

**Note 6.** Heading 5907 does not apply to: (a) fabrics in which the impregnation, coating or covering cannot be seen with the naked eye; (b) fabrics painted with designs (other than painted canvas being theatrical scenery, studio back-cloths or the like); (c) fabrics partially covered with flock, dust, powdered cork or the like and bearing designs resulting from these treatments (imitation pile fabrics remain in this heading); (d) fabrics finished with normal dressings having a basis of amylaceous or similar substances; (e) wood veneered on a backing of textile fabrics (heading 4408); (f) natural or artificial abrasive powder or grain, on a backing of textile fabrics (heading 6805); (g) agglomerated or reconstituted mica, on a backing of textile fabrics (heading 6814); or (h) metal foil on a backing of textile fabrics (generally section XIV or XV).

**Note 7.** Heading 5910 does not apply to: (a) transmission or conveyor belting, of textile material, of a thickness of less than 3 mm; or (b) transmission or conveyor belts or belting of textile fabric impregnated, coated, covered or laminated with rubber or made from textile yarn or cord impregnated, coated, covered or sheathed with rubber (heading 4010).

**Note 8.** Heading 5911 applies to the following goods, which do not fall in any other heading of section XI: (a) textile products in the piece, cut to length or simply cut to rectangular (including square) shape (other than those having the character of the products of headings 5908 to 5910), the following only: (i) textile fabrics, felt and felt-lined woven fabrics, coated, covered or laminated with rubber, leather or other material, of a kind used for card clothing, and similar fabrics of a kind used for other technical purposes, including narrow fabrics made of velvet impregnated with rubber, for covering weaving spindles (weaving beams); (ii) bolting cloth; (iii) filtering and straining cloth of a kind used in oil presses or the like, of textile material or of human hair; (iv) flat woven textile fabrics with multiple warp or weft, whether or not felted, impregnated or coated, of a kind used in machinery or for other technical purposes; (v) textile fabric reinforced with metal, of a kind used for technical purposes; (vi) cords, braids and the like, whether or not coated, impregnated or reinforced with metal, of a kind used in industry as packing or lubricating materials; (b) textile articles (other than those of headings 5908 to 5910) of a kind used for technical purposes (for example, textile fabrics and felts, endless or fitted with linking devices, of a kind used in papermaking or similar machines (for example, for pulp or asbestos-cement), gaskets, washers, polishing discs and other machinery parts).

tariffUpdates.h1: HTS Chapter 59: Coated Fabrics, Tire Cord & Industrial Textiles — Tariff Updates

seo.title: HTS Chapter 59 Tariff Updates 2026: Coated Fabric, Tire Cord & Technical Textile Duties Since January 2025 | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What changed for HTS Chapter 59 — coated and laminated fabrics, tire cord, conveyor belts, technical textiles — since January 2025: the end of the IEEPA and Section 122 duties, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs (India +10%, Vietnam +12.5%, EU 10%), China List 3, Canada Section 338 and the antidumping orders, with Federal Register citations.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). **No Chapter 59 base rate changed**: all 75 lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates, from Free to 14.1%.

Everything that changed sits on top of the base rate. In 2025 the IEEPA duties reached coated fabrics and technical textiles from every country — 20% for Vietnam and 15% in total for the EU from August 7, 2025, 50% for India from August 27, and up to 145% for China in April–May 2025, on top of the 25% List 3 duty. The IEEPA duties **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff**: +10% for India, Cambodia and the UK, +12.5% for Vietnam, Turkey and Israel, 10% in total for the EU and Taiwan, 12.5% in total for Japan and South Korea. China still pays the **25% List 3 duty** on 74 of the 75 lines (7.5% List 4A on the other). Since **August 22, 2026** four Chapter 59 subheadings from Canada pay a **50% Section 338 duty**, even under USMCA. The antidumping orders on Chinese artist canvas, Chinese and Taiwanese narrow woven ribbons and Chinese and Vietnamese laminated woven sacks remain in force; Commerce set an 83.67% rate for two Taiwanese ribbon exporters on September 4, 2026.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 59 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, the China Section 301 List 3 and List 4A duties, the Canada Section 338 duties, Russia's rates in lieu of column 2, and the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended. Antidumping and countervailing duty orders whose scope can reach Chapter 59 subheadings are listed as reference entries. No Section 232 product action lists a Chapter 59 line. Preference-program changes (GSP, AGOA) are listed for reference. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

changes.title: No Chapter 59 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 75 Chapter 59 lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates in 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition, and no line was added, split or renumbered.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 3 and List 4A continue after the four-year review
changes.detail: USTR announced that the 2018–2019 China Section 301 actions did not terminate on their 2026 anniversaries because domestic industries asked for them to continue. For Chapter 59 this keeps +25% (List 3) on 74 lines and +7.5% (List 4A) on 5903.10.15.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 lists revised; Chapter 59 entries unchanged
changes.detail: Proclamations 11064 and 11065 added and removed provisions on the 9903.03.12 and 9903.03.14 lists. The four Chapter 59 subheadings on the 9903.03.14 list are the same in 2026 Revision 18 (before) and Revision 21 (after).

changes.title: Antidumping review: narrow woven ribbons from Taiwan
changes.detail: Commerce set an 83.67% dumping margin for Lace Fashions Industrial Co. and Trydent Co. for September 2023–August 2024. The order covers narrow woven ribbons with woven selvedge, which may also enter under 5903.90.10, 5903.90.25, 5903.90.3090, 5907.00.60 and 5907.00.80; the written scope, not the HTS number, decides coverage.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duty takes effect on four Chapter 59 subheadings
changes.detail: 50% on listed products of Canada after a 3-day suspension lapsed. Chapter 59 is on the motor-vehicle list (9903.03.14): plastic-coated man-made-fiber fabrics 5903.90.25 and other plastic-coated fabrics 5903.90.30, other coated man-made-fiber fabrics 5907.00.60 and other technical textiles 5911.90.00. Unlike the Section 301 duty, it applies to USMCA-qualifying goods too (U.S. note 51(a)).

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies cover all of Chapter 59
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84). No Chapter 59 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). EU and Taiwanese goods pay 10% in total, Japanese and Korean goods 12.5% in total. India, Cambodia and the UK +10%; Vietnam, Turkey and Israel +12.5%. Jordanian goods and CAFTA-DR goods from Guatemala and El Salvador are exempt on every Chapter 59 subheading except 5906.10.00 (note 52(j)). USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94).

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: 25% on all goods of Brazil (9903.05.01). No Chapter 59 line is on the Brazil exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii)). From July 24 the 12.5% forced-labor tariff (9903.05.27) is added on top.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) still remove the base rate and the Section 301 duty on Mexican and most Canadian Chapter 59 goods.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. No Chapter 59 subheading was on the product exemption list (9903.03.03). USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico, and duty-free CAFTA-DR textile and apparel goods, were exempt.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China, Brazil and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: India's extra 25% IEEPA duty removed
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% duty on products of India (9903.01.84) from February 7, 2026. The 25% reciprocal rate on India ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24.

changes.title: AGOA reauthorized through December 31, 2026
changes.detail: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 renewed AGOA retroactively from September 30, 2025. In Chapter 59, AGOA (SPI D) is printed on five lines — PVC- and other plastic-coated cotton fabric (5903.10.10, 5903.90.10), rubberized adhesive tape (5906.10.00), man-made-fiber belts (5910.00.10) and filter cloth (5911.40.01). GSP (SPI A, A*) remains expired since December 31, 2020.

changes.title: Scheduled: Section 301 tariff on products of Nicaragua
changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that pay the column 1-general rate (that is, not entered under CAFTA-DR) will pay +10% (9903.89.01) from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028. Today Nicaragua pays the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty (9903.05.58).

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.24) fell from +20% to +10%. It ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84), on top of the 25% reciprocal rate in force since August 7, 2025 (EO 14326): 50% in all on Indian coated fabrics, on top of the base rate. Ended February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Country reciprocal rates replace the 10% baseline
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 set country rates for goods entered from August 7, 2025: Cambodia, Indonesia and Thailand +19%, Vietnam +20%, India +25%, the UK +10%. EU goods with a column 1 rate under 15% paid 15% in total (9903.02.20) — every Chapter 59 line. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional 40% IEEPA duty on products of Brazil
changes.detail: Executive Order 14323 added 40% on Brazilian goods on top of the 10% reciprocal duty. Ended February 24, 2026; replaced from July 22, 2026 by the 25% Brazil Section 301 tariff.

changes.title: Canada additional duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: Raised the IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods to +35% (9903.01.10). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty cut from 125% to 10%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14298 cut the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 10% for goods entered from May 14, 2025. Chinese PU-coated fabric (7.5% base) then paid 7.5% + 25% (List 3) + 20% + 10% = 62.5% until November 9, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty raised to 125%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14266 raised the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 125% from April 10, 2025, and paused the higher country rates announced on April 2 for other countries. With the 20% fentanyl duty and the 25% List 3 duty, Chinese PU-coated fabric paid 177.5% until May 13, 2025.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) from April 5, 2025, and country rates (9903.02.xx); Canada and Mexico excluded. No Chapter 59 product was on the exemption annex. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.20, then 9903.01.24) went from +10% (from February 4, 2025) to +20%, on top of the List 3 duty. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Antidumping and countervailing orders on laminated woven sacks from China continued
changes.detail: After the third sunset review the orders continue from February 20, 2025. Unfinished sacks in roll form may be classified in 5903.90.25. A Vietnam order on the same product was continued from November 20, 2024.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.01); USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.04). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Canada
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.10), later raised to +35%; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.14). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Antidumping order on artist canvas from China continued
changes.detail: The order (A-570-899) covers primed or coated artist canvases — pre-stretched canvases, canvas panels, pads and rolls — classifiable in 5901.90.20, 5901.90.40, 5903.90.10, 5903.90.20, 5903.90.25, 5907.00.60 and 5907.00.80. Tracing cloth and paint-by-number canvases are excluded. Commerce listed it again among open orders on June 2, 2026.

changes.title: Antidumping and countervailing orders on narrow woven ribbons continued
changes.detail: The China (AD and CVD) and Taiwan (AD) orders on narrow woven ribbons with woven selvedge, up to 12 cm wide, continue. Covered ribbons may enter under Chapter 59 subheadings 5903.90.10, 5903.90.25, 5907.00.60 and 5907.00.80.

changes.title: China List 4A duty cut to 7.5%
changes.detail: The List 4A duty (9903.88.15), in force from September 1, 2019 at 15%, was cut to 7.5%. In Chapter 59 List 4A covers only 5903.10.15 (PVC-coated layered man-made-fiber fabric over 60% plastics).

changes.title: China List 3 duty raised to 25%
changes.detail: USTR raised the List 3 duty (9903.88.03) from 10% to 25%. List 3 covers every Chapter 59 subheading except 5903.10.15, and the rate has applied ever since.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 3 reaches coated fabrics and technical textiles
changes.detail: The third China Section 301 list put +10% on Chinese coated and laminated fabrics, tire cord, linoleum, wall coverings, wicks, hose, belts and technical textiles (headings 5901–5911).

changes.title: Antidumping orders on industrial belts revoked
changes.detail: Commerce revoked the 1989 antidumping orders on industrial belts from Germany, Italy, Singapore and Japan, whose HTS list included 5910.00.10 and 5910.00.90, effective January 1, 2000. No order on Chapter 59 belts has been issued since.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 59 goods were **$2.86B in 2025**, 8.8% less than the $3.13B of 2024 and below the $3.28B peak of 2022. Two headings carry most of it: **plastic-coated fabrics (5903)**, $1.03B, and **technical textiles (5911)**, $964M. The single largest product is **5911.90 — gaskets, machinery parts and other technical textile articles** ($644M), followed by other plastic-coated fabrics (5903.90, $445M) and **polyester tire cord fabric** (5902.20, $190M).

**Mexico** ($485M) is the largest supplier, almost all of it 5911 technical textiles ($401M) — goods that can enter free under USMCA. **India** ($315M, -7.6%) more than doubled since 2020 ($141M) and leads in coated fabrics ($262M of 5903). **China** fell 27.6% to $284M, from $371M in 2020. **Vietnam** ($252M) supplies most U.S. tire cord fabric imports ($185M of $298M). Canada ($290M), Japan ($160M), Germany ($157M) and South Korea ($116M) follow; Germany and Italy lead in textile conveyor belts (5910).

The figures are annual and stop at 2025, before the 2026 tariff changes (the end of the IEEPA duties in February, the Section 301 tariffs from July 24, 2026 and the Canada Section 338 duties from August 22); they do not show what those changes did. Duty-collected figures are not available from an official source yet.

industryAreas.intro:
Chapter 59 base rates run from Free to 14.1%, and the extra duty **depends on where the goods come from**. Each cell below is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duty for that country, minus any preference — taken from the current tariff schedule.

Since the IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026, the extra duty is mainly the **Section 301 tariff on 60 economies** that started July 24, 2026: **+10% for India, Cambodia and the UK**, **+12.5% for Vietnam, Turkey and Israel**, **10% in total for Germany, Italy, the Netherlands and the rest of the EU and for Taiwan**, and **12.5% in total for Japan and South Korea**. **China adds 37.5%** (12.5% plus the 25% List 3 duty). USMCA-qualifying goods from Mexico pay nothing; from Canada they pay nothing except on the **four subheadings with the 50% Section 338 duty**, which no USMCA claim removes.

The country exception lists in note 52(j) cover every Chapter 59 8-digit subheading except 5906.10.00 for Jordan (9903.06.20), and for Guatemala (9903.06.06) and El Salvador (9903.06.09) when entered under CAFTA-DR; the Cambodia, Malaysia, Indonesia, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Argentina, Ecuador, EU, UK and other lists name no Chapter 59 line. The Brazil list (note 50(a)(ii)) has no Chapter 59 line. China: List 3 (note 20(f)) covers every subheading except 5903.10.15, which is on List 4A (note 20(i)); the List 3 exclusions printed in note 20 for some coated fabrics (5901.90.40, 5903.10.20, 5903.20.20, 5903.20.25, 5903.90.20) have expired, and none of the exclusions in effect (note 20(vvv)) is in Chapter 59; no line is on the 2024 increases of note 31. tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 59: Coated Fabrics, Tire Cord & Industrial Textiles — Import Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Coated Fabrics, Tire Cord & Industrial Textiles into the U.S.: Origin Rules, Labeling, AD/CVD & Legal Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 59) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What each HTS Chapter 59 line needs at U.S. entry — textile origin rules and manufacturer ID, country-of-origin marking, FTC textile labeling, antidumping scopes for artist canvas and ribbons — and the legal ways to pay less: plastic-content classification, origin, USMCA, FTAs, first sale, drawback, FTZ and rulings.

tariffEngineering.intro:
Chapter 59 goods need no import license, but they are **textile products** under CBP's origin rules: their country of origin — which decides the extra duty — is generally where the **fabric was formed**, not where it was coated, laminated or cut (19 CFR 102.21), and every entry must name the manufacturer with a manufacturer identification code (19 CFR 102.23). Goods must be marked with their country of origin. Coated fabrics, belts and artists' canvases are outside the FTC textile labeling rules, but uncoated fabrics sold for household use are not. Primed artist canvas from China, narrow woven ribbons from China and Taiwan and laminated woven sack fabric from China and Vietnam can owe **antidumping or countervailing duties**.

On cost, the **plastic content and coating** decide the rate (a PU-coated man-made-fiber fabric pays 7.5%, the same fabric over 70% plastics by weight is Free), the **country of origin** decides the extra duty (+10% India, 10% in total EU, +37.5% China), and USMCA, FTAs, first-sale valuation, drawback and foreign-trade zones lower the bill further. Each lever depends on a document, listed below with its regulation.

levers.title: Classify by coating, fiber and plastic content
levers.saves: The gap between 5903 and 5906 lines: a man-made-fiber fabric coated with PVC, PU or other plastics pays 7.5% (8% or 14.1% for Section XI note 9 layered fabrics), but Free when it is over 70% rubber or plastics by weight (over 60% plastics for note 9 fabrics); cotton-based coated fabric pays 2.7%
levers.appliesTo: Headings 5903, 5906 and 5907 — coated, laminated and rubberized fabrics
levers.document: Technical data showing the fiber, the coating polymer, the weight share of plastics or rubber and whether the coating is visible, on one or both sides.
levers.caveat: Fabrics fully embedded in plastics, coated on both sides or too stiff to bend around a 7 mm cylinder are plastics of Chapter 39, and an invisible coating leaves the fabric in Chapters 50–55, 58 or 60 (Chapter 59 note 2). The declared classification must match the goods; a ruling settles doubtful cases.

levers.title: Know the country of origin — where the fabric was formed
levers.saves: The difference between country rates: +10% for India, 10% in total for the EU, +12.5% for Vietnam, +37.5% for China
levers.appliesTo: All lines; the gap is widest on coated fabrics and tire cord from China
levers.document: Production records showing where the base fabric was woven or knitted (the "fabric-making process") and where any finishing took place; for hose and belts with non-textile parts, where they were wholly assembled.
levers.caveat: Coating, laminating, dyeing or cutting a fabric in a second country generally does not change its origin; for 5901–5903, 5905 and 5906–5907 finishing confers origin only when the fabric is both dyed and printed with two or more other finishing operations. The Section 301 and 338 duties follow the country of origin, and CBP can ask for proof.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20, 51, 52

levers.title: Claim USMCA on goods from Mexico or Canada
levers.saves: The base rate (up to 14.1%) plus the 10% Section 301 duty
levers.appliesTo: All lines from Mexico; from Canada, every line except 5903.90.25, 5903.90.30, 5907.00.60 and 5911.90.00
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, kept ready for CBP.
levers.caveat: USMCA does not remove the 50% Section 338 duty on the four Canadian subheadings in U.S. note 51(b)(3). The good must meet the Chapter 59 rule of origin in General Note 11 for its subheading. The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

citations.label: HTSUS General Note 11 (USMCA rules of origin)

levers.title: Claim an FTA, AGOA or CBERA preference
levers.saves: The base rate, and for CAFTA-DR goods from Guatemala or El Salvador — and all Jordanian goods — the Section 301 duty too (except on 5906.10.00)
levers.appliesTo: Dutiable lines whose Special column lists the program: Korea (KR), Israel (IL), CAFTA-DR (P), Jordan (JO), Colombia, Peru, Chile and the other FTA partners, CBERA (E, E*) and, on five lines, AGOA (D)
levers.document: The origin proof each program requires (a certification or declaration of origin, or the AGOA or CBERA documentation) and records to back it up.
levers.caveat: An FTA removes the base rate but, except where a note 52(j) list says otherwise, not the 2026 Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(a)) — Korean and Israeli goods still pay 12.5%. AGOA runs to December 31, 2026. GSP (A, A*) has been expired since December 31, 2020, although its codes are still printed.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a), (j)

levers.title: Value at the first sale for export when you buy through a middleman
levers.saves: Every ad valorem duty is charged on a lower value — the base rate and the 10%–50% extra duties included — when the mill price to a trading company is lower than the price you pay
levers.appliesTo: All lines bought through a trading company or agent rather than straight from the mill
levers.document: Proof that the first sale was a bona fide sale for export to the United States at arm's length: the mill invoice, contracts and payment records.
levers.caveat: Only a sale clearly destined for the U.S. qualifies, and the importer must be able to show the earlier price at entry.

levers.title: Recover duty on goods you export or use in exported products
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid, when the imported fabric (or goods made from it, such as tires, belts or upholstered seats) is exported or destroyed
levers.appliesTo: Any line — for example tire cord built into tires or coated fabric sewn into products shipped abroad
levers.document: A drawback claim to CBP with import, manufacturing and export records.
levers.caveat: Claims have filing deadlines and record-keeping rules; check whether a given Chapter 99 duty is eligible before relying on it.

levers.title: Use a foreign-trade zone
levers.saves: No duty on goods re-exported from the zone, and duty deferred until goods leave it for the U.S. market
levers.appliesTo: Any line — useful for fabric and belting used in production for export
levers.document: Zone admission (CBP Form 214) and the zone operator's inventory records.
levers.caveat: Goods entered for U.S. consumption from a zone pay the duties in force on the entry date.

levers.title: Use a Chapter 98 provision for U.S. goods coming back
levers.saves: All duty on U.S.-made goods returned unchanged (9801.00.10), for example belts or felts sent back from a foreign customer
levers.appliesTo: Any line, for American goods returned without having been advanced in value or improved abroad
levers.document: Proof of U.S. origin and of the export, as CBP requires for the provision.
levers.caveat: The Section 301 and 338 duties also do not apply to goods properly entered under Chapter 98, except subchapter XXIII and 9802.00.40–9802.00.80 (U.S. notes 51(a) and 52(a)).

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 51(a), 52(a)

levers.title: Get a binding classification or scope ruling
levers.saves: Certainty where the line decides the rate and the extra duty: 5903 versus Chapter 39; 5910 textile belt versus 4010 rubber belt; a fabric on or off the Canada Section 338 list; and whether a canvas or ribbon falls inside an antidumping order
levers.appliesTo: Any line where the material, construction or use decides the line
levers.document: A ruling request to CBP describing the fabric, coating, weights and use; for antidumping scope, a scope ruling application to Commerce.
levers.caveat: Rulings apply to the transaction described; a changed construction may need a new one. The written scope of an antidumping order, not the HTS number, decides coverage.

rules.title: Chapter 59 goods are "textile products": origin follows the specific rules for headings 5901–5911 — generally the country where the fabric was formed; coating or laminating alone does not confer origin
Every commercial entry of textile products must identify the manufacturer (the maker that performed the origin-conferring operation) with a manufacturer identification code
Country-of-origin marking in English, legible, indelible and permanent enough to reach the ultimate purchaser — on the goods or, for rolls and bulk fabric, their container or tag
Invoices for textile fiber products must state the fiber content by weight, the manufacturer's FTC identification and the country where processed or manufactured

Textile Fiber Products Identification Act: uncoated fabrics sold for household use need fiber-content, origin and dealer labels; coated fabrics, belts and artists' canvases, and industrial articles not listed in the rule, are excluded

Antidumping and countervailing cash deposits: primed artist canvas from China (5901.90, some 5903.90 and 5907.00); narrow woven ribbons from China and Taiwan (may enter under 5903.90 and 5907.00); laminated woven sack fabric in rolls from China and Vietnam (5903.90.25). Coverage follows the written scope

rules.title: Report the Chapter 99 headings with the line: the 2026 Section 301 heading for the country (or its note 52(j) exemption), China List 3 (9903.88.03) or List 4A (9903.88.15), Brazil (9903.05.01), Canada Section 338 (9903.03.14), Russia (9903.90.08)

groups.note: Primed artist canvas from China (5901.90.20, 5901.90.40) is under antidumping order A-570-899; tracing cloth and paint-by-number canvases are excluded. Artists' canvases are outside the FTC labeling rule.

groups.label: Tire cord fabric of nylon, polyester or rayon
groups.note: Tire cord fabric is not on the Section 232 automobile-parts list (note 33(g)). Origin is where the cord fabric was woven.

groups.label: Fabrics coated or laminated with plastics (PVC, PU — incl. faux leather)
groups.note: The plastic content decides the line: Free above 70% plastics (60% for note 9 fabrics). 5903.90.25 and 5903.90.30 from Canada pay the 50% Section 338 duty even under USMCA; 5903.10.15 is the only China List 4A line. Coated fabrics are outside the FTC labeling rule. Some canvas, ribbon and woven-sack-fabric shipments fall under antidumping orders.

groups.label: Linoleum & floor coverings on a textile backing
groups.note: Linoleum is Free from every column 1 country; only the extra duty by country applies.

groups.label: Textile wall coverings
groups.note: Wall coverings must be in rolls at least 45 cm wide (note 4); flock on paper is heading 4814.

groups.label: Rubberized fabrics & rubberized adhesive tape
groups.note: 5906.10.00 rubberized adhesive tape is the one line not on the Jordan and CAFTA-DR exception lists. Rubber-coated belts are heading 4010, not 5906 or 5910.

groups.label: Other coated fabrics & painted theatrical scenery
groups.note: 5907.00.60 from Canada pays the 50% Section 338 duty even under USMCA. Painted theatrical scenery is Free.

groups.label: Textile wicks & gas mantle fabric
Textile hose (fire hose and similar tubing)
groups.note: Hose with metal fittings or armor takes its origin from where it was wholly assembled.

groups.label: Textile conveyor & transmission belts
groups.note: Belts of rubber-coated fabric and belting under 3 mm thick are not here (note 7). The 1989 antidumping orders on industrial belts were revoked in 2000.

groups.label: Technical textiles: paper-machine clothing, bolting cloth, filter cloth, printers' blankets
groups.note: 5911.90.00 from Canada pays the 50% Section 338 duty even under USMCA. Paper-machine felts and forming fabrics are 5911.31–5911.32.

faqs.question: What does HTS Chapter 59 cover?
faqs.answer: Chapter 59 covers textile fabrics impregnated, coated, covered or laminated with plastics (5903), rubber (5906), gum or starch (5901) or other materials (5907); tire cord fabric (5902); linoleum (5904); textile wall coverings (5905); wicks (5908); textile hose (5909); conveyor and transmission belts (5910); and technical textiles such as paper-machine felts, bolting cloth, filter cloth and printers' blankets (5911). Its 75 lines carry base rates from Free to 14.1%. U.S. imports were $2.86B in 2025.

faqs.question: What are the tariffs on coated fabric from China?
searchedAs: tariffs on fabric from china to usa
us tariff on china for fabrics
faqs.answer: Chinese Chapter 59 goods pay the base rate plus 12.5% (2026 Section 301, 9903.05.31) plus 25% (List 3, 9903.88.03): 45% on PU- or PVC-coated man-made-fiber fabric (7.5% base), 51.6% on layered PVC fabric of 5903.10.18, 43.3% on nylon or polyester tire cord, 41.5% on man-made-fiber conveyor belts. 5903.10.15 is on List 4A instead (+7.5%), for 20% in total. Primed artist canvas also owes antidumping duty. China supplied $284M in 2025, 27.6% less than in 2024.

faqs.question: What are the U.S. tariffs on coated fabric and textiles from India?
searchedAs: tariff on textiles from india to usa
us tariffs on textiles from india
faqs.answer: Since July 24, 2026 Indian Chapter 59 goods pay the base rate plus 10% Section 301 (9903.05.44): 17.5% for PU- or PVC-coated man-made-fiber fabric, 18% for laminated or PU note 9 fabrics, 12.7% for coated cotton fabric, 15.8% for tire cord. The IEEPA duties on India — 50% from August 27, 2025 — ended in February 2026. India supplied $315M in 2025, most of it coated fabric.

faqs.question: Are there tariffs on fabric from Canada?
searchedAs: are there tariffs on fabric from canada
faqs.answer: USMCA-qualifying Chapter 59 goods from Canada pay no base duty and no Section 301 duty — except four subheadings on the Section 338 list (5903.90.25, 5903.90.30, 5907.00.60 and 5911.90.00), which pay 50% since August 22, 2026 even under USMCA. Goods that do not qualify pay the base rate plus 10% (plus 50% on those four). Canada supplied $290M of Chapter 59 goods in 2025.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for PVC or PU coated fabric?
searchedAs: hs code for pvc coated fabric
hs code of pu coated fabric
faqs.answer: Fabrics coated or laminated with plastics are heading 5903: with PVC 5903.10, with polyurethane 5903.20, with other plastics 5903.90. For man-made-fiber fabric the U.S. line depends on the plastic content: over 70% plastics by weight 5903.10.20, 5903.20.20 or 5903.90.20 (Free); otherwise 5903.10.25, 5903.20.25 or 5903.90.25 (7.5%). Coated cotton is 5903.10.10, 5903.20.10 or 5903.90.10 (2.7%). A fabric coated on both sides or completely embedded in plastics is Chapter 39.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for synthetic or faux leather?
searchedAs: hs code for pu synthetic leather
faqs.answer: Faux leather made of a knitted or woven textile base coated on one side with PU or PVC is heading 5903 — usually 5903.20.25 (PU, 7.5%) or 5903.10.25 (PVC, 7.5%), or Free under 5903.20.20 / 5903.10.20 when plastics are over 70% of the weight. Fabric completely embedded in plastics or coated on both sides, and cellular plastic sheet where the fabric only reinforces, are Chapter 39 (Chapter 59 note 2). Finished bags of synthetic leather are heading 4202.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for tire cord fabric?
faqs.answer: Tire cord fabric of high-tenacity yarn is heading 5902: nylon or other polyamides 5902.10.00.00 (5.8%), polyesters 5902.20.00.00 (5.8%), other (viscose rayon) 5902.90.00.00 (Free). From Vietnam, the largest supplier, polyester tire cord pays 18.3% in total; from China 43.3%. Tire cord fabric is not on the Section 232 auto-parts list.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for a conveyor belt or V-belt?
searchedAs: hs code for pvc conveyor belt
hs code for rubber conveyor belt
faqs.answer: Conveyor and transmission belts of textile material, including those coated with plastics such as PVC, are heading 5910: 5910.00.10 for man-made fibers (4%; V-belts .10.10, synchronous belts .10.20, belting .10.60–.70) and 5910.00.90 for other fibers (2.6%). Belts of rubber-coated fabric or rubberized cord, and belting under 3 mm thick, are not here: rubber belts are heading 4010.

faqs.question: What does HS code 5911 cover?
faqs.answer: Heading 5911 covers textile products for technical uses: rubber-coated card clothing and printers' blankets (5911.10, 2.9%–3.8%), bolting cloth and screen-printing fabric (5911.20, Free–3.3%), paper-machine felts and forming fabrics (5911.31 under 650 g/m², 5911.32 650 g/m² or more, 3.8%), filter cloth for oil presses (5911.40, 8%) and other technical articles such as gaskets and packing cords (5911.90, 3.8%). 5911.90.00 from Canada pays the 50% Section 338 duty.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for filter cloth?
faqs.answer: Filtering and straining cloth of a kind used in oil presses or the like, including that of human hair, is 5911.40.01.00 (8%). Other industrial filter fabrics in the piece of a kind used for technical purposes are usually 5911.90.00 (3.8%), and made-up filter bags can be 5911.90 too. Plain fabrics with no technical character stay in Chapters 50–55 or 60.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for artist canvas, and is there an antidumping duty?
faqs.answer: Prepared painting canvas is 5901.90.20.00 (man-made fibers, 7%) or 5901.90.40.00 (cotton and other, 4.1%). Primed artist canvas from China — stretched canvases, panels, pads and rolls — is also under antidumping order A-570-899, continued in 2022. Printed canvas art is Chapter 49 or 97, and canvas bags heading 4202.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for cloth adhesive tape?
searchedAs: hs code for self adhesive tape
faqs.answer: Rubberized textile adhesive tape not over 20 cm wide is 5906.10.00.00 (2.9%). Tapes with a plastic backing are Chapter 39 (3919), and paper tapes Chapter 48. 5906.10.00 is the one Chapter 59 line not on the Jordan and CAFTA-DR Section 301 exception lists.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for linoleum and textile wall coverings?
searchedAs: hs code for textile wall covering
faqs.answer: Linoleum is 5904.10.00.00 and other floor coverings of a coating on a textile backing 5904.90; textile wall coverings in rolls at least 45 cm wide are 5905.00. All are Free from column 1 countries, so only the extra duty by country applies — 10% in total from the EU or the UK, 37.5% from China. Vinyl flooring is Chapter 39.

faqs.question: What are the HS codes for fire hose and candle wick?
searchedAs: hs code for fire hose pipe
faqs.answer: Textile fire hose and similar tubing is heading 5909: 5909.00.10.00 of vegetable fibers (Free) or 5909.00.20.00 of other fibers (3.3%). Woven, plaited or knitted wicks for candles, lamps, stoves and lighters are 5908.00.00.00 (3.4%). Rubber hose is Chapter 40.
